label: Congress 107

definitions.speech: Attributed non-procedural spoken words; turns and active days provide context.
definitions.sponsored: Distinct H.R. and S. bills for which the member is the official sponsor.
definitions.passed: Sponsored bills with an official measure-level House or Senate passage action.
definitions.enacted: Sponsored bills with an assigned public or private law number.
definitions.profanity: Unquoted curated profanity hits per 100,000 attributed words.

caveats: Speech counts include only remarks attributable to a specific member by Bioguide ID; procedural speech, submitted Extensions of Remarks, and material printed into the Record are excluded.
Profanity uses a conservative, hand-curated list rather than an exhaustive dictionary. Passages marked as quotations are excluded from a member's rate and retained as a separate audit count.
A member's most-used profanity term is the most frequent accepted, unquoted surface form in the selected period; alphabetical order breaks ties. It does not imply personal preference.
Members below the word threshold are omitted from the profanity ranking because rates computed from small samples are unstable.
Legislative counts cover sponsored House and Senate bills (H.R. and S.) only; cosponsorships, resolutions, and amendments are outside this version.
A sponsored bill passing or becoming law is descriptive. It does not establish that one member personally caused the outcome or measure legislative effectiveness by itself.
The Congressional Record is lightly edited rather than verbatim, and source metadata can be corrected after publication.

profanity.label: Profanity
profanity.definition: Unquoted matches from a narrow, curated profanity list.

hostility.label: Personal hostility / disrespect
hostility.definition: Curated personal attack and disrespect terms.

misconduct.label: Misconduct allegations
misconduct.definition: Curated language alleging corruption, abuse, or other misconduct.

language.trend_alt: Monthly Democratic and Republican rates for profanity, personal hostility or disrespect, and misconduct allegations in Congress 107.
language.member_alt: Highest eligible member rates for profanity, personal hostility or disrespect, and misconduct allegations in Congress 107.

explanation.shown: The charts show monthly Democratic and Republican rates for three separate lexical measures, plus the highest-rate members in Congress 107. Rates are hits per 100,000 attributed spoken words.
explanation.examined: The trend panels compare party-wide rates over time. Member panels show the highest nonzero rates among speakers with substantial floor remarks.
explanation.finding: Democratic and Republican aggregate profanity rates are approximately equal at 0.1 per 100,000 words. Mr. FILNER has the highest eligible profanity rate at 4.4 per 100,000 words. Republicans have the higher aggregate personal hostility / disrespect rate (2.6 versus 2.2 per 100,000 words). Mr. DIAZ-BALART has the highest eligible personal hostility / disrespect rate at 24.4 per 100,000 words. Democrats have the higher aggregate misconduct allegations rate (7.0 versus 6.4 per 100,000 words). Mr. LEVIN has the highest eligible misconduct allegations rate at 64.2 per 100,000 words.
explanation.limitation: These are descriptive word-pattern counts, not judgments about intent. Misconduct language does not prove misconduct, and quoted profanity is excluded from a speaker's rate.
